task: Make cross-crate ownership rejection reach the intended semantic invariant
observation: The inherited EffectProvider fixture declared Item as a struct and matched it using enum patterns. A live moss check of the original fixture reports MATCH_REQUIRES_ENUM at line 7, so its provider could never build to test source-free consume/read rejection. Replacing Item with an exported enum and named Resource payload makes the provider pass structured Moss checking.
impact: An unrelated invalid fixture previously hid whether imported ownership summaries were preserved and could be misclassified as missing compiler support.

resolution.summary: Use a valid exported enum for the ownership fixture. Source-free acceptance still fails on prep compiler ABI-v9 output, accurately preserving the remaining integration dependency.

task: Exercise real source-removed ABI-v10 scenarios before production-default cutover
observation: An explicit staged-v10 harness mode on the S/H candidate changed an old ABI-v9-only 0 PASS / 1 BLOCKED / 10 FAIL result into 8 PASS / 0 BLOCKED / 3 FAIL with real provider removal and executable consumers. It exposed two invalid fixture return annotations and a mutation that previously changed the discoverable module name before validation.
impact: Candidate ABI transport and two independently typed consumers can now be tested without changing the production default. The remaining failures are localized to third-crate generic nominal forwarding, an exact missing-method diagnostic, and layout/cache invalidation.
evidence: debug staged run: scenarios 1,2,3,5,6,8,9,10 PASS; 4,7,11 FAIL

resolution.summary: Harness/fixture corrections are in the source-free branch; three compiler-facing failures and same-SHA PR validation remain.
